monuments.name: Stonehenge
monuments.construction_date: Multi-stage, c. 3000-1600 BC; sarsen circle/trilithons erected c. 2620-2480 cal BC (95% prob., Bayesian model) [S1]
monuments.spread_note: Antler-pick and ditch/posthole-fill radiocarbon, Bayesian-modelled across stages spanning ~3000-1600 BC
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried sarsen/bluestone stone-hole packing surfaces if re-excavated
monuments.decisive_if: Direct OSL/exposure dates on stone-socket surfaces would confirm or revise whether erection matches the antler-pick dates

sources.citation: Darvill, T., Marshall, P., Parker Pearson, M., Wainwright, G. (2012). Stonehenge remodelled. Antiquity 86(334): 1021-1040.
Parker Pearson, M. (2021). Archaeology and legend: investigating Stonehenge. Archaeology International 24(1).

monuments.notes: Textbook associated-organic case: many dates, sealed contexts, decades of Bayesian refinement, but no date has ever been taken from the stones themselves.

monuments.name: Avebury
monuments.construction_date: Main henge bank/ditch c. 2500 cal BC; precise date of the stone circles themselves unresolved [S1]
monuments.spread_note: Source states reliable dates for construction phases 'remain scarce'; stone-circle date not independently fixed
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried megalith stone-hole packing (Southern/Northern Inner Circles)
monuments.decisive_if: A direct date on stone-hole fill would show whether the megaliths are contemporary with, or postdate, the c. 2500 BC bank

sources.citation: Gillings, M., Pollard, J., Strutt, K. (2019). The origins of Avebury. Antiquity 93(368): 359-377.

monuments.notes: Authors themselves flag the chronology as poorly secured; a striking direct quote from the paper: reliable dates 'remain scarce'.

monuments.name: Newgrange
monuments.construction_date: Charcoal from burnt-soil roof-joint caulking gave GrN-5462 2550+/-45 BC and GrN-5463 2465+/-40 BC (uncalibrated, as published 1969); widely recalibrated in later literature to c. 3200 cal BC, not independently re-verified in this audit [S1]
monuments.n_dates: 2 (original 1969 study); later dating programmes reportedly added more, not independently confirmed here
monuments.spread_note: Only 2 primary dates, but charcoal was sealed in roof-joint caulking under 3m of undisturbed cairn material
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: U-series on any calcite/flowstone over passage orthostats; OSL of buried orthostat bases
monuments.decisive_if: More direct/sealed dates would confirm the ~3200 cal BC estimate and pin sub-phases (kerb vs chamber vs cairn)

sources.citation: O'Kelly, M.J. (1969). Radiocarbon Dates for the Newgrange Passage Grave, Co. Meath. Antiquity 43(170): 140-141.
Cooney, G. (2006). Newgrange - a view from the platform. Antiquity 80(309): 697-708.

monuments.notes: Good example of a calibration-driven age shift: the original 1969 paper's uncalibrated ~2500 BC became the famous 'older than the Pyramids' ~3200 cal BC once calibration curves matured; only the primary 1969 figures were read directly in this audit.

monuments.name: Carrowmore
monuments.construction_date: 4th-millennium BC per revised antler/bone-pin dating; earlier claims of a 5th-millennium BC (Mesolithic-adjacent) origin now considered unreliable [S1]
monuments.n_dates: 25 (new pin-fragment dates from 2 monuments, Bergh & Hensey 2013)
monuments.spread_note: 25 new pin dates revise earlier charcoal-based 5th-millennium-BC claims to a 4th-millennium-BC range
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: None on the stones; further antler/bone dating from sealed cairn contexts at undated monuments in the complex
monuments.decisive_if: Would settle whether Carrowmore genuinely predates or postdates other Irish passage tombs such as Newgrange

sources.citation: Bergh, S., Hensey, R. (2013). Unpicking the Chronology of Carrowmore. Oxford Journal of Archaeology 32(4): 343-366.

monuments.notes: A clean vindication of H7's logic in reverse: the paper explicitly names 'the general problem of using charcoal to date megalithic monuments' as the cause of earlier overestimates.

monuments.name: Callanish Stones
monuments.construction_date: Erected in the later Neolithic, commonly cited as c. 2900 BC in secondary literature; precise construction-context dating not confirmed in sources read this audit [S1]
monuments.n_dates: few (not enumerated in the source checked at citation level only)
monuments.spread_note: Dating leans on peat-inception and pit/posthole radiocarbon rather than dated material from the stone sockets
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried stone-socket packing if sockets are re-excavated
monuments.decisive_if: A direct date on stone-socket fill would test whether erection matches the commonly cited ~2900 BC estimate

sources.citation: Richards, C., Demetri, G., French, C., Nunn, R. et al. (2013). Expedient Monumentality. In Building the Great Stone Circles of the North, pp. 224-253.

monuments.notes: Only verified at citation level (paywalled, abstract not available via OpenAlex); construction-date figure is a commonly cited estimate, flagged as not independently confirmed in this audit's reading.

monuments.name: Ring of Brodgar
monuments.construction_date: Later Neolithic, commonly cited c. 2600 BC; no organic material recovered in direct association with the stone sockets themselves [S1]
monuments.n_dates: very few (ditch-cut dating only, per chapter title/abstract-level review)
monuments.spread_note: Chronology rests mainly on ditch-cut dates; the standing stones themselves are undated
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of stone-socket packing if re-excavated; U-series if any carbonate crust is present
monuments.decisive_if: A direct date on a stone socket would confirm whether the ~2600 BC ditch-based estimate applies to the stones

sources.citation: Downes, J., Richards, C., Brown, J., Cresswell, A.J. et al. (2013). Investigating the Great Ring of Brodgar, Orkney. In Building the Great Stone Circles of the North, pp. 90-118.

monuments.notes: Only verified at citation level (paywalled). A strong H7 lead: Orkney's other great monuments (Ness of Brodgar) are well dated, but Brodgar's own stones reportedly are not.

monuments.name: Carnac alignments
monuments.construction_date: Morbihan megalith-building emerges c. 4700-4300 cal BC per regional Bayesian model; the alignments' own individual menhirs are not separately dated in the source read [S1]
monuments.n_dates: 2,410 radiocarbon results compiled region-wide; count specific to the alignment rows not stated
monuments.spread_note: Huge regional dataset (n=2410) pins the wider tradition, but few if any dates tie directly to individual alignment stone-sockets
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried menhir-socket packing; excavation of unexcavated alignment sockets
monuments.decisive_if: Direct dates on alignment stone-sockets would show if the rows are contemporary with regional tomb-building or a later addition

sources.citation: Schulz Paulsson, B. (2019). Radiocarbon dates and Bayesian modeling support maritime diffusion model for megaliths in Europe. PNAS 116(9): 3460-3465.

monuments.notes: Regional strength should not be mistaken for site-specific strength: the 2410-date Bayesian model covers NW-France megaliths broadly, not the Carnac alignments' individual stones specifically.

monuments.name: Barnenez cairn
monuments.construction_date: c. 4800 BC, among the earliest known megalithic monuments in Europe, from charcoal in the cairn matrix [S1][S2]
monuments.n_dates: several from the original excavation, incorporated into a larger regional Bayesian dataset
monuments.spread_note: Charcoal dates from the cairn matrix place Barnenez among the earliest European megaliths, ~4800 BC
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried orthostat/chamber-wall contact surfaces
monuments.decisive_if: Would test whether Barnenez is truly among the very earliest European megaliths or whether charcoal dates reflect old wood

sources.citation: Giot, P., l'Helgouach, J. (1957). Le Cairn de Barnenez en Plouezoc'h (Finistere). Architecture et mobilier de la tombe C. Annales de Bretagne.
Schulz Paulsson, B. (2019). Radiocarbon dates and Bayesian modeling support maritime diffusion model for megaliths in Europe. PNAS 116(9): 3460-3465.

monuments.notes: Original 1957 excavation report verified at citation level only (pre-DOI-era French journal); charcoal-in-matrix is a classic 'old wood' risk the source does not appear to address.

monuments.name: Dolmen of Menga
monuments.construction_date: c. 3800-3600 BCE, per recent geoarchaeological/engineering studies [S1][S2]
monuments.n_dates: not stated in the passages read; papers assert the date range without detailing the underlying radiocarbon dataset
monuments.spread_note: Narrow 200-year range cited by 2 recent papers, but the dating evidence itself (likely skeletal remains/pottery) was not directly confirmed here
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried capstone/orthostat foundation contact surfaces (foundation depths already geoarchaeologically mapped by the source team)
monuments.decisive_if: Would confirm whether capstone-laying matches the currently cited 3800-3600 BCE range

sources.citation: Lozano Rodriguez, J.A., Garcia Sanjuan, L., Jimenez-Espejo, F.J., Alvarez-Valero, A.M. et al. (2024). Early science and colossal stone engineering in Menga, a Neolithic dolmen (Antequera, Spain). Science Advances 10(34).

Rodriguez, J.A.L., Sanjuan, L.G., Alvarez-Valero, A.M., Jimenez-Espejo, F. et al. (2023). The provenance of the stones in the Menga dolmen reveals one of the greatest engineering feats of the Neolithic. Scientific Reports 13(1).

monuments.notes: Abstracts and full-text passages read focus on engineering/quarry provenance, not the radiocarbon basis for the quoted date; a paywall (science.org, HTTP 403) blocked deeper full-text access to the chronology section. Flagged as a verification gap rather than papered over.

monuments.name: Almendres Cromlech
monuments.construction_date: UNVERIFIED precise date; secondary literature commonly places it in the Middle Neolithic (broadly 6th-5th millennium BC), but no dedicated radiocarbon/OSL dating study of the cromlech itself was located in this audit
monuments.n_dates: 0 (no absolute dates for this monument found)
monuments.spread_note: No radiocarbon/OSL/U-series dates for the cromlech itself found in this audit; age rests on regional stylistic comparison
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried menhir-base contact surfaces; excavation for sealed organic material at stone bases
monuments.decisive_if: Any direct or associated date at all would be a first for this monument and could confirm or overturn the assumed Middle Neolithic age

sources.citation: Cerrillo-Cuenca, E., Bueno-Ramirez, P. et al. (2019). '3DMeshTracings': A protocol for the digital recording of prehistoric art. Its application at Almendres cromlech (Evora, Portugal). Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports.

monuments.notes: Search for a dedicated Almendres chronology/OSL paper (e.g. Boaventura-led work on Alentejo menhirs) did not surface a citable result within this audit's tool budget. This is one of the cleanest H7 cases in the sample: apparently no absolute date exists for the monument at all.

monuments.name: Ggantija
monuments.construction_date: c. 3600-3200 BC (Ggantija phase of the Maltese temple sequence), per the calibrated radiocarbon chronology Renfrew established for Malta's temple period [S1]
monuments.n_dates: several, defining Malta's island-wide temple-period phases; dataset is the original 1960s-70s one, not independently re-checked here
monuments.spread_note: Phase-defining dates underpinning 'Ggantija phase' terminology are decades old; no recent site-specific re-dating confirmed
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: U-series on any calcite deposits on temple walls; OSL of buried orthostat bases
monuments.decisive_if: Fresh direct/associated dating would test whether the 1970s temple-phase boundaries still hold

sources.citation: Renfrew, C. (1972). Malta and the calibrated radiocarbon chronology. Antiquity 46(182): 141-144.

monuments.notes: A more recent island-wide Bayesian re-dating project (e.g. FRAGSUS) is known to exist in the literature but a citable DOI/abstract for it was not located within this audit's search budget; flagged rather than assumed.

monuments.name: Hagar Qim
monuments.construction_date: c. 3600-3200 BC per the island-wide Maltese temple-period sequence; no temple-specific dating dataset located in this audit [S1]
monuments.n_dates: not specific to this temple in sources reviewed; relies on the island-wide temple-period framework
monuments.spread_note: No temple-specific radiocarbon dataset found; dated by fitting into Malta's general sequence, not by direct evidence from the site
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried megalith bases; U-series on any carbonate crusts on the stones
monuments.decisive_if: A site-specific date would show whether Hagar Qim fits the standard island sequence or needs its own chronology

sources.citation: Renfrew, C. (1972). Malta and the calibrated radiocarbon chronology. Antiquity 46(182): 141-144.

monuments.notes: Same source-scarcity issue as Ggantija; both Maltese temples share this audit's weakest source base for a 'mainstream, well-known' monument.

monuments.name: Gobekli Tepe
monuments.construction_date: c. 9600-8200 cal BC; e.g. lime-mortar sample KIA-44149: 9984+/-42 BP = 9745-9314 cal BC; latest Pre-Pottery-Neolithic activity 8860+/-60 BP = 8240-7780 cal BC [S1]
direct_methods_applied: mortar/plaster radiocarbon (AMS on lime mortar and embedded organics, Kiel lab)
monuments.n_dates: many (dozens of AMS dates across Layers III/II)
monuments.spread_note: Mortar and charcoal AMS dates span ~9745-7780 cal BC across construction/use phases
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: Already applied (mortar radiocarbon); further dating of individual enclosure fills could refine sub-phasing
monuments.decisive_if: Already largely settled by direct mortar dates; further dates would refine sequencing between enclosures, not the overall age

sources.citation: Dietrich, L., Meister, J., Dietrich, O., Notroff, J., Kiep, J., Heeb, J., Beuger, A., Schutt, B. (2019). Cereal processing at Early Neolithic Gobekli Tepe, southeastern Turkey. PLOS ONE 14(5): e0215214.
Schmidt, K. (2000). Gobekli Tepe, Southeastern Turkey. A Preliminary Report on the 1995-1999 Excavations. Paleorient 26(1): 45-54.

monuments.notes: The one clear counter-example to H7 in this batch of 20: construction is dated directly via radiocarbon on the lime mortar itself, not merely on associated finds.

monuments.name: Karahan Tepe
monuments.construction_date: Broadly PPNA/early PPNB (10th-9th millennium BC), dated mainly by comparison to Gobekli Tepe; no site-specific radiocarbon dataset located in this audit [S1]
monuments.n_dates: 0 confirmed in sources reviewed (comparison-based dating only in the accessible literature found)
monuments.spread_note: 2011 report dates the site by stylistic comparison (T-pillar motifs) to Gobekli Tepe only
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: Mortar/lime-plaster radiocarbon as successfully applied at Gobekli Tepe, if comparable material is present
monuments.decisive_if: Direct mortar or sealed-fill dates would confirm whether Karahan Tepe is contemporary with, older, or younger than Gobekli Tepe

sources.citation: Celik, B. (2011). Karahan Tepe: a new cultural centre in the Urfa Area in Turkey. Documenta Praehistorica 38: 241-254.

monuments.notes: Important gap to flag: large-scale controlled excavation under Necmi Karul since 2019 (Tas Tepeler project) almost certainly has produced radiocarbon dates, but a citable DOI/abstract for that later work was not located within this audit's search budget. The record above reflects only the earlier, style-comparison-based literature found.

monuments.name: Nevali Cori
monuments.construction_date: UNVERIFIED specific dates; general literature places the PPNB cult building broadly in the 9th millennium BC, but no primary dating source was independently confirmed in this audit
monuments.n_dates: UNVERIFIED - not independently confirmed in this audit
monuments.spread_note: UNVERIFIED - primary excavation reports (Hauptmann, largely pre-DOI German-language publications) not accessed this audit
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: None now feasible - site has been submerged under the Ataturk Dam reservoir since 1992
monuments.decisive_if: N/A for new fieldwork; only re-analysis of archived samples/records from the 1980s-90s excavation could refine this

sources.citation: Nevali Cori. (2021). Encyclopedic Dictionary of Archaeology, p. 931.

monuments.notes: The weakest-sourced record in this batch. Primary Nevali Cori publications (Hauptmann's excavation reports) are largely pre-DOI German-language journal articles (Istanbuler Mitteilungen, Anatolica) not indexed on Crossref/OpenAlex; none were located via this audit's search tools. Flagged honestly rather than filled in from unverified general knowledge, per project no-fabrication rule.

monuments.name: Rujm el-Hiri
monuments.construction_date: Chalcolithic period per a recent OSL-supported landscape analysis, contra earlier Early Bronze Age attributions based on surface pottery [S1][S2]
monuments.n_dates: few sherds plus an OSL study (sample count not stated in the abstract read)
monuments.spread_note: Few sherds gave inconsistent Early-Bronze-ish dates; a newer OSL study instead argues for the Chalcolithic
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: OSL of buried wall-base contact surfaces (already partly applied); further sampling of wall foundations
monuments.decisive_if: More OSL/associated dates would resolve the long-standing Chalcolithic-vs-Early-Bronze-Age dispute

sources.citation: Freikman, M., Porat, N. (2017). Rujm el-Hiri: The Monument in the Landscape. Tel Aviv 44(1): 14-39.
Freikman, M. (2018). Dating the Megalithic Structures of the Golan. Journal of the Israel Prehistoric Society 48: 108-146.

monuments.notes: Source explicitly states 'there is still no consensus on its date...due to the very scanty archaeological evidence found between its walls' - a direct, citable confirmation of H7's premise.

monuments.name: Baalbek (Temple of Jupiter podium and trilithon)
monuments.construction_date: Conventionally Julio-Claudian, c. AD 40-60, anchored by a stonemason's graffito dated 2 August AD 60 on one of the blocks; relative sequence of trilithon vs podium still debated [S1]
monuments.n_dates: n/a (one securely dated inscription; broader phasing inferred from Roman textual/architectural context)
monuments.spread_note: One dated mason's graffito (AD 60) anchors the podium; the trilithon's relative sequence is still debated
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: None applicable to the dry-laid megalithic core (no mortar); cosmogenic exposure dating of quarry-face cut surfaces could be tried
monuments.decisive_if: Would resolve whether the trilithon predates, postdates, or is contemporary with the Julio-Claudian podium construction

sources.citation: Magli, G. (2019). The Archaeoastronomy and Chronology of the Temple of Jupiter at Baalbek. In Archaeoastronomy in the Roman World, pp. 145-151.

monuments.notes: Source itself states 'an impressive number of problems remain unsolved...including precise dating, phases of construction'; a dated graffito is unusually strong for the historical-contextual category, but per the audit's own schema an inscription is text, not a physical dating method.

monuments.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
monuments.construction_date: Conventionally attributed to Khafre (4th Dynasty, c. 2500 BC) via stylistic/facial and causeway-layout association with Khafre's pyramid complex; a minority geological weathering argument (Schoch) proposes a much greater age, contested by mainstream geologists reading the same outcrop differently [S1][S2][S3]
monuments.n_dates: 0 (no radiometric/absolute date of the carved bedrock itself)
monuments.spread_note: No absolute date of the carved bedrock exists; age is inferred from art style and causeway alignment to Khafre's complex
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: Cosmogenic nuclide exposure dating of enclosure-wall carved surfaces; U-series on any calcite veining
monuments.decisive_if: A direct exposure/U-series date could confirm the Khafre-era attribution, or support a substantially older or younger carving date

sources.citation: Dobecki, T.L., Schoch, R.M. (1992). Seismic investigations in the vicinity of the great Sphinx of Giza, Egypt. Geoarchaeology 7(6): 527-544.
Chowdhury, A.N., Punuru, A.R., Gauri, K.L. (1990). Weathering of limestone beds at the great sphinx. Environmental Geology and Water Sciences 15(3): 217-223.
The Geology of the Great Sphinx. (2026). In Rewriting the History of the Great Sphinx, pp. 125-147.

monuments.notes: The canonical H7 case in this batch: both the mainstream dating and the best-known challenge to it rest on interpretation (style, or weathering-pattern reading) rather than any absolute chronometric date of the bedrock.

monuments.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
monuments.construction_date: c. 2560-2540 BC (4th Dynasty, reign of Khufu), from radiocarbon on organic material (charcoal, reed, wood) embedded in mortar/construction debris, broadly matching but offset from the historical regnal chronology [S1][S2]
monuments.n_dates: many (450+ organic samples collected across Old/Middle Kingdom monuments; subset specific to the Great Pyramid)
monuments.spread_note: Radiocarbon dates trend somewhat older than the historical/regnal chronology by decades to about a century (old-wood effect debated)
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: Direct mortar-carbonate radiocarbon (distinct from dating organic inclusions) rarely attempted due to old-carbon contamination risk in Egyptian lime
monuments.decisive_if: Would test whether the radiocarbon/historical offset reflects old wood, mortar reuse/repair, or a genuine chronology revision

sources.citation: Bonani, G., Haas, H., Hawass, Z., Lehner, M. et al. (2001). Radiocarbon Dates of Old and Middle Kingdom Monuments in Egypt. Radiocarbon 43(3): 1297-1320.
Bronk Ramsey, C., Dee, M.W. et al. (2010). Radiocarbon-Based Chronology for Dynastic Egypt. Science 328(5985): 1554-1557.

monuments.notes: Classified as associated-organic rather than direct: the dated material is organic temper/debris embedded in or under the mortar, not radiocarbon on the mortar's own lime carbonation (a distinct, rarely-used technique for Egyptian contexts). This distinction is judgment-call territory and worth a specialist's review.

monuments.name: Osireion, Abydos
monuments.construction_date: Conventionally linked to Seti I's adjacent temple, c. 1290s-1279 BC (19th Dynasty), by location/architectural association and inscriptions in the neighbouring temple and later additions; the megalithic core itself carries no independent inscriptional date [S1]
monuments.spread_note: No radiocarbon/OSL/U-series dates located for the structure; dated purely by proximity to Seti I's temple and later royal additions
monuments.feasible_direct_methods: U-series on calcite deposited during the structure's long groundwater submersion; OSL of buried foundation-block contact surfaces
monuments.decisive_if: A direct date would settle whether the Osireion's core is contemporary with Seti I or an earlier/later structure later associated with his temple

sources.citation: Wegner, M.P. (2019). Birth and Rebirth in the Abydos Landscape. In Abydos, pp. 235-254.

monuments.notes: Along with the Great Sphinx and Almendres, one of this batch's cleanest H7 leads: zero absolute dates located for a megalithic structure whose age is debated partly on the basis of construction style resembling earlier (Old Kingdom) masonry.
